title: jd-resume-tailor fact bank
description: A bank of work entries and projects whose bullets, scope notes and optional structured facts are the only things a tailored resume may say. Unknown fields are rejected on purpose: a misspelled scope or bullet_capabilities would otherwise be ignored without a word, and scope carries the DO NOT CLAIM limits.

github.description: Link to the public code, if there is any.
github.x-error: must be an http(s) URL without spaces

has_code.description: Whether the code can be shown. Only projects with code are candidates for a resume.

id.description: Letters, digits, '_' and '-'. No '#', which separates an entry id from a fact number.
id.x-error: must be letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting and ending with a letter or digit

bullets.description: The original bullets. Each one is a fact the resume may restate, and the sentence the tool falls back to when a rewrite fails verification. LaTeX escapes are allowed.

bullet_capabilities.description: One short capability label per bullet, in the same order.

adaptable.description: False means the bullets may only be copied verbatim. Defaults to true.

scope.description: Provenance and limits, in free text. Labelled parts such as 'EVIDENCE:' are allowed. The text after 'DO NOT CLAIM:' (up to the next label) lists what a bullet must not say, one claim per semicolon or sentence. 'Same project as <id>.' marks entries that describe one project.

facts.description: Optional structured facts. When present they replace the bullets as what a bullet may cite; without them each bullet is a fact of its own.

id.description: Unique across the whole bank. The ids '<entry id>#<n>' and '<entry id>#scope' are what an entry without facts gets, so they are taken.
id.x-error: must start with a letter or digit and use only letters, digits, '_', '.', '#' and '-'

unit.description: For example 'ms', '%', 'x', 'req/s', 'users'; an empty string for a bare count.

as_measured.description: The number exactly as it was recorded, with its formatting and precision, for example '0.875' or '3,781'. A JSON number cannot keep the trailing zeros or the thousands separator that tell how precise the measurement was.
